```{r setup, include=FALSE}
project_root <- if (file.exists("R/cwd_model_selection.R")) "." else ".."
result_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data",
  "site_level",
  "fluxnet_cwd_model_selection.rds"
)
has_results <- file.exists(result_path)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 110,
  eval = has_results,
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(tricolore)

if (has_results) {
  result <- readRDS(result_path)
  site_order <- sort(result$site_selection$sitename)
}

tricolore_hue <- 0.35
tricolore_breaks <- 4L
tricolore_chroma <- 1
tricolore_lightness <- 1
tricolore_contrast <- 0.999
model_vertices <- data.frame(
  energy = c(1, 0, 0),
  storage = c(0, 1, 0),
  recharge = c(0, 0, 1)
)
model_colors <- setNames(
  Tricolore(
    model_vertices,
    "energy", "storage", "recharge",
    breaks = tricolore_breaks,
    hue = tricolore_hue,
    chroma = tricolore_chroma,
    lightness = tricolore_lightness,
    contrast = tricolore_contrast,
    legend = FALSE
  ),
  c("energy", "energy_storage", "energy_recharge")
)
decision_colors <- c(
  favours_a = "#0072B2",
  favours_b = "#D55E00",
  indistinguishable = "#B8B8B8",
  both_rejected = "#7B3294"
)
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      # ggtern registers these as relative theme elements; setting them here
      # keeps ordinary ggplot2 panels valid with ggplot2 >= 4.0 as well.
      tern.axis.ticks.length.major = rel(1),
      tern.axis.ticks.length.minor = rel(0.5)
    )
)
```

<style>
.site-table {
  max-height: 32rem;
  overflow-y: auto;
  margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
}
.site-table table { width: 100%; }
.tab-content { padding-top: 1rem; }

  border-left: 4px solid #0072B2;

This analysis compares three deliberately compact hypotheses for interannual
variation in the annual maximum CWD at each FLUXNET site. Each hypothesis is
fitted to the full annual record and every pair is compared with a parametric
bootstrap likelihood-ratio contrast. Leave-one-year-out predictions are kept
as a complementary check on predictive skill.

## Annual data used for inference

The analysis unit is one site-year. For year $t$:

- $D_t$ is the annual maximum CWD calculated from observed ET;
- $P_t$ is the annual maximum PCWD calculated with the site's calibrated
  PET; and
- $R_{t-1}$ is the maximum of the latest CWS event whose peak occurs on or
  before the date of $D_t$.

Thus, $t-1$ denotes the preceding recharge event, not necessarily the
previous calendar year. All quantities are in millimetres. Each retained site
has at least 10 complete annual triples.

## Candidate models

The three observation models are

$$
\begin{aligned}
  A:\quad D_t &= aP_t + e_t,\\
  B:\quad D_t &= \min(aP_t,S_0) + e_t,\\
  C:\quad D_t &= \min(aP_t,bR_{t-1}) + e_t.
\end{aligned}
$$

There is no additive intercept. The physical parameters satisfy
$a\geq0$, $b\geq0$, and $S_0\geq0$. For likelihood calculation,
$e_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_m^2)$. Every candidate is calibrated separately,
including its own residual-error standard deviation $\sigma_m$.

```{r model-definitions}
model_table <- result$model_definitions |>
  transmute(
    Model = model_label,
    `Mean structure` = model_formula,
    `Limiting mechanisms` = mechanism_count,
    `Mean parameters` = fitted_parameter_count
  )

knitr::kable(model_table, digits = 2)
```

Model A estimates $a$ by non-negative zero-offset least squares. Model B
profiles the PCWD threshold corresponding to $S_0/a$, refits $a$ at every
trial threshold, and reports the cap on the response scale as $S_0$. Model C
profiles the ratio $b/a$ over all intervals where the limiting branch is
unchanged and refits $a$ at every trial value; it then recovers
$b=a(b/a)$. These profile searches give the global minimum residual sum of
squares for the piecewise models. An unused cap is represented by infinity,
so B or C can reduce exactly to A without assigning an arbitrary finite limit.

## Pairwise parametric-bootstrap likelihood tests

For a pair labelled model A and model B, the observed signed likelihood-ratio
contrast is

$$
  T_{B-A}=2\{\ell_B(\widehat\theta_B)-
                 \ell_A(\widehat\theta_A)\}.
$$

Positive values indicate a larger maximized likelihood for B; negative values
indicate a larger likelihood for A. For each pair, the analysis performs two
directional parametric-bootstrap tests:

1. Fit A to all annual observations. Simulate `r result$bootstrap_replicates`
   annual response series from its fitted means and Gaussian residual
   distribution, refit both A and B to every series, and form
   $T^*_{B-A}$. The right-tail probability
   $p_A=\Pr_A(T^*_{B-A}\geq T_{B-A})$ measures evidence against A in the
   direction of B.
2. Repeat with B as the generating model. The left-tail probability
   $p_B=\Pr_B(T^*_{B-A}\leq T_{B-A})$ measures evidence against B in the
   direction of A.

The predictors are held fixed in the simulations; all regression parameters,
including $a$, $b$, $S_0$, and $\sigma_m$, are re-estimated in every
replicate. The Monte Carlo
p-values use the finite-simulation correction
$(1+\text{tail count})/(1+B)$. The decision threshold is
$\alpha=`r result$bootstrap_alpha`$.

```{r model-pairs}
pair_table <- result$model_pairs |>
  transmute(
    Pair = pair_label,
    A = model_a_id,
    B = model_b_id,
    Structure = comparison_type
  )
knitr::kable(pair_table)
```

The energy model is a boundary case of both capped models: B reduces to A as
$S_0\rightarrow\infty$, and C reduces to A as $b\rightarrow\infty$. The
storage- and recharge-cap models are non-nested. A standard chi-squared LRT
reference distribution is therefore not used. Calibrating the signed contrast
under both fitted generating models puts all three pairs on the same footing
and avoids treating either non-nested model as an arbitrary default null.

The possible pairwise outcomes are:

- reject A only: evidence favours B;
- reject B only: evidence favours A;
- reject neither: the annual record does not distinguish the pair; or
- reject both: neither fitted generating model reproduces the observed
  contrast, a warning about model misspecification rather than a winner.

## Parsimonious selection and predictive check

A model decisively favoured in a pair defeats the other member. The site-level
selection is made among candidates that are not decisively defeated in any of
their two comparisons. If several remain, the order is: fewest physical
mechanisms, fewest fitted mean parameters, smallest AICc. Thus, an added limit
is retained only when the bootstrap evidence is sufficient to remove a simpler
candidate. The selected class summarizes this rule; the pairwise p-values and
likelihood contrasts remain the primary evidence.

Leave-one-year-out cross-validation (LOYO-CV) is also performed. For each held-
out year, all parameters are fitted on the other years before predicting the
annual maximum CWD. CV RMSE is not used as the formal selection gate here; it
shows whether a full-record likelihood preference also translates into stable
out-of-sample prediction.

<div class="model-note">
The bootstrap uses the full annual record but is conditional on the fitted
Gaussian model and fixed PCWD/CWS predictors. It does not propagate uncertainty
from PET calibration or the construction of annual water-balance summaries.
With `r result$bootstrap_replicates` replicates, the smallest attainable
Monte Carlo p-value is `r signif(1 / (result$bootstrap_replicates + 1), 3)`.
</div>

## Network-wide results

```{r selection-counts, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.2}
selection_counts <- result$site_selection |>
  count(selected_model_id, selected_model_label, name = "sites") |>
  right_join(
    result$model_definitions |>
      select(selected_model_id = model_id, selected_model_label = model_label),

  mutate(sites = replace_na(sites, 0L)) |>
  arrange(sites) |>
  mutate(

  geom_col(width = 0.7) +

```

The next plot retains the four possible outcomes rather than forcing a winner.

```{r decision-counts, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
decision_labels <- c(
  favours_a = "Favours A",
  favours_b = "Favours B",
  indistinguishable = "No distinction",
  both_rejected = "Both rejected"
)
decision_counts <- result$pairwise_tests |>
  count(pair_label, decision_code, name = "sites") |>
  complete(
    pair_label = result$model_pairs$pair_label,
    decision_code = names(decision_labels),
    fill = list(sites = 0L)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    decision = factor(
      decision_labels[decision_code],
      levels = unname(decision_labels)
    )
  )

ggplot(decision_counts, aes(sites, pair_label, fill = decision_code)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = decision_colors,
    breaks = names(decision_labels),
    labels = unname(decision_labels),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(x = "Number of sites", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

The discrete color map uses LOYO-CV mean squared error to represent relative
predictive skill. For model $m$, define

$$
  w_m = \frac{1/\mathrm{CV\text{-}MSE}_m}
              {\sum_j 1/\mathrm{CV\text{-}MSE}_j}.
$$

The three weights lie between zero and one and sum to one. Along an edge that
compares models X and Y, Y's conditional coordinate is

$$
  q_{Y\mid XY}=\frac{w_Y}{w_X+w_Y}
              =\frac{\mathrm{MSE}_X}{\mathrm{MSE}_X+\mathrm{MSE}_Y}.
$$

Thus, zero favours X, one favours Y, and 0.5 represents equal predictive skill.
These are descriptive skill weights, not posterior model probabilities. The
bootstrap tests above continue to determine whether the observed differences
are sufficient to distinguish models.

```{r tricolore-skill-data, include=FALSE}
skill_long <- result$model_performance |>
  group_by(sitename) |>
  mutate(
    inverse_cv_mse = 1 / pmax(cv_mse_mm2, .Machine$double.eps),
    relative_skill = inverse_cv_mse / sum(inverse_cv_mse)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

skill_map <- skill_long |>
  select(sitename, model_id, relative_skill) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model_id, values_from = relative_skill) |>
  left_join(
    result$site_selection |>
      select(sitename, selected_model_id, selected_model_label),
    by = "sitename"
  ) |>
  arrange(selected_model_id, sitename)

skill_tricolore <- Tricolore(
  skill_map,
  p1 = "energy",
  p2 = "energy_storage",
  p3 = "energy_recharge",
  center = rep(1 / 3, 3),
  breaks = tricolore_breaks,
  hue = tricolore_hue,

  lightness = tricolore_lightness,
  contrast = tricolore_contrast,
  spread = 1,
  show_data = TRUE,
  show_center = TRUE,
  label_as = "pct",
  crop = FALSE
)
skill_map$skill_rgb <- skill_tricolore$rgb
rgb_channels <- t(grDevices::col2rgb(skill_map$skill_rgb)) / 255
skill_map$text_color <- ifelse(
  0.2126 * rgb_channels[, 1] +
    0.7152 * rgb_channels[, 2] +
    0.0722 * rgb_channels[, 3] > 0.58,

  "white"
)
skill_map <- skill_map |>
  mutate(
    tile_index = row_number() - 1L,
    tile_column = tile_index %% 6L + 1L,
    tile_row = tile_index %/% 6L + 1L
  )
```

The triangle uses the same discrete `{tricolore}` scale with four margins
along every axis. Maximum chroma and tip lightness give saturated cyan,
magenta, and yellow vertices, while maximum contrast keeps the equal-skill
center black. White points with black outlines and directly connected labels
keep individual sites visible across both light and dark cells.

```{r tricolore-skill-key, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
ternary_xy <- function(p1, p2, p3) {
  data.frame(
    x = p3 + 0.5 * p2,
    y = sqrt(3) / 2 * p2
  )
}

ternary_mesh <- function(k) {
  triangles <- vector("list", k^2)
  cell <- 0L
  for (p1_integer in 0:(k - 1L)) {
    for (p2_integer in 0:(k - 1L - p1_integer)) {
      p3_integer <- k - p1_integer - p2_integer
      cell <- cell + 1L
      triangles[[cell]] <- data.frame(
        cell = cell,
        vertex = 1:3,
        p1 = c(p1_integer, p1_integer + 1L, p1_integer) / k,
        p2 = c(p2_integer, p2_integer, p2_integer + 1L) / k,
        p3 = c(p3_integer, p3_integer - 1L, p3_integer - 1L) / k
      )
      if (p3_integer >= 2L) {
        cell <- cell + 1L
        triangles[[cell]] <- data.frame(
          cell = cell,
          vertex = 1:3,
          p1 = c(p1_integer + 1L, p1_integer + 1L, p1_integer) / k,
          p2 = c(p2_integer, p2_integer + 1L, p2_integer + 1L) / k,
          p3 = c(p3_integer - 1L, p3_integer - 2L, p3_integer - 1L) / k
        )
      }
    }
  }
  bind_rows(triangles[seq_len(cell)])
}

key_mesh <- ternary_mesh(tricolore_breaks)
key_centers <- key_mesh |>
  group_by(cell) |>
  summarise(
    p1 = mean(p1),
    p2 = mean(p2),
    p3 = mean(p3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
key_centers$cell_color <- Tricolore(
  key_centers,
  "p1", "p2", "p3",
  center = rep(1 / 3, 3),
  breaks = tricolore_breaks,
  hue = tricolore_hue,
  chroma = tricolore_chroma,
  lightness = tricolore_lightness,
  contrast = tricolore_contrast,
  spread = 1,
  legend = FALSE
)
key_mesh <- key_mesh |>
  left_join(select(key_centers, cell, cell_color), by = "cell")
key_mesh <- bind_cols(
  key_mesh,
  ternary_xy(key_mesh$p1, key_mesh$p2, key_mesh$p3)
)

key_points <- bind_cols(
  skill_map,
  ternary_xy(skill_map$energy, skill_map$energy_storage,
             skill_map$energy_recharge)
)

grid_values <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)
key_grid <- bind_rows(lapply(grid_values, function(value) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(axis = "energy", value, endpoint = 1:2,
               p1 = value, p2 = c(0, 1 - value),
               p3 = c(1 - value, 0)),
    data.frame(axis = "storage", value, endpoint = 1:2,
               p1 = c(0, 1 - value), p2 = value,
               p3 = c(1 - value, 0)),
    data.frame(axis = "recharge", value, endpoint = 1:2,
               p1 = c(0, 1 - value), p2 = c(1 - value, 0),
               p3 = value)
  )
})) |>
  group_by(axis, value) |>
  mutate(
    x = ternary_xy(p1, p2, p3)$x,
    y = ternary_xy(p1, p2, p3)$y,
    xend = rev(x),
    yend = rev(y)
  ) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(key_mesh, aes(x, y, group = cell, fill = cell_color)) +
  geom_polygon(color = NA) +
  geom_segment(
    data = key_grid,
    aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.35,
    color = scales::alpha("black", 0.55)
  ) +
  geom_polygon(fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    data = key_points,
    aes(x, y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    size = 4.2,
    stroke = 1,
    fill = "white",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = key_points,
    aes(x, y, label = sitename),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    seed = 42,
    size = 2.4,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black",
    fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.9),
    box.padding = 0.18,
    point.padding = 0.22,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    max.iter = 50000,
    max.time = 5,
    linewidth = 0.2,
    segment.color = "grey20",
    segment.size = 0.25
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.03, y = -0.035, label = "Energy A",
           hjust = 1, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = sqrt(3) / 2 + 0.045,
           label = "Storage cap B", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.03, y = -0.035, label = "Recharge cap C",
           hjust = 0, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.12, 1.12), ylim = c(-0.07, 0.96), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Relative out-of-sample skill by site",
    subtitle = "Labels are displaced for legibility; leader lines identify the site points"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey30"),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 24, 8, 24)
  )
```

## Per-site diagnostics

Each tab compares held-out predictions from all three tested models for one
site, using the same axis limits and year colors across panels. Each panel is
titled with its model and reports its own out-of-sample $R^2$ and RMSE. The
selected model is labelled explicitly and highlighted with a blue border.
Observed CWD is on the y-axis. The $R^2$ comes from
leave-one-year-out cross-validation,
$R^2_{\mathrm{CV}}=1-\sum_t(D_t-\widehat D_{t,-t})^2/
\sum_t(D_t-\overline D)^2$. Because every prediction is held out, this value
can be negative when a model predicts less well than the observed
site mean.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r site-tabs, results='asis', fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, out.width='100%'}
for (site in site_order) {
  site_selection <- result$site_selection |>
    filter(sitename == site)
  site_cv_predictions <- result$cv_predictions |>
    filter(sitename == site)
  model_diagnostics <- site_cv_predictions |>
    group_by(model_id) |>
    summarise(
      total_sum_squares = sum((observed_cwd_mm - mean(observed_cwd_mm))^2),
      residual_sum_squares = sum((observed_cwd_mm - predicted_cwd_mm)^2),
      cv_rmse_mm = sqrt(mean((observed_cwd_mm - predicted_cwd_mm)^2)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    left_join(result$model_definitions, by = "model_id") |>
    mutate(
      model_order = match(model_id, result$model_definitions$model_id),
      selected = model_id == site_selection$selected_model_id,
      cv_r_squared = if_else(
        total_sum_squares > 0,
        1 - residual_sum_squares / total_sum_squares,
        NA_real_
      ),
      r_squared_text = if_else(
        is.finite(cv_r_squared), sprintf("%.2f", cv_r_squared), "not defined"
      ),
      model_title = paste0(
        LETTERS[model_order], ": ", model_label, "\n",
        if_else(selected, "SELECTED MODEL", "Candidate model"), "\n",
        sprintf("LOYO-CV R² = %s; RMSE = %.1f mm", r_squared_text, cv_rmse_mm)
      )
    ) |>
    arrange(model_order) |>
    mutate(model_title = factor(model_title, levels = model_title))
  site_cv_predictions <- site_cv_predictions |>
    left_join(
      model_diagnostics |> select(model_id, model_title),
      by = "model_id"
    )

  cat("\n### ", site, "\n\n", sep = "")
  plot_limits <- range(
    site_cv_predictions$observed_cwd_mm,
    site_cv_predictions$predicted_cwd_mm,
    0
  )
  fit_plot <- ggplot(
    site_cv_predictions,
    aes(predicted_cwd_mm, observed_cwd_mm, color = year)
  ) +
    geom_rect(
      data = model_diagnostics |> filter(selected),
      aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      fill = NA,
      color = "#0072B2",
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dotted",
      linewidth = 0.7,
      color = "grey35"
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(
      option = "D",
      end = 0.9,
      breaks = range(site_cv_predictions$year),
      labels = range(site_cv_predictions$year),
      guide = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 9)
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(model_title), nrow = 1) +
    coord_equal(xlim = plot_limits, ylim = plot_limits) +
    labs(
      title = site,
      x = "Held-out model prediction (mm)",
      y = "Observed annual maximum CWD (mm)",
      color = "Year",
      caption = "Dotted line: 1:1; every plotted prediction is out of sample"
    ) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines")
    )
  print(fit_plot)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

## Interpretation guardrails

The pairwise results measure relative support among these three observation
models; they do not establish a unique causal mechanism. A recharge cap cannot
be identified when preceding CWS nearly always exceeds PCWD. A storage cap is
weakly identified when few annual PCWD values bracket its fitted threshold.
Because the models have no intercept, systematic proportional or additive
discrepancies must appear in $a$, $b$, $S_0$, or the residuals. A scale at zero
means there is no positive fitted relationship and should not be interpreted
mechanistically. An infinite fitted opposing scale denotes an inactive,
unidentified cap rather than an extremely large estimated physical parameter.

The bootstrap treats annual residuals as independent and Gaussian. Serial
dependence, uncertainty in CWD/PCWD/CWS, and selection among many sites are not
included in the reported p-values. “No supported distinction” is therefore an
appropriate substantive result for short records, not evidence that the two
models are identical.
